span.term: TWO EXPLANATIONS OF THE PAPER'S CENTRAL FINDING ARE OFFERED AND NEITHER IS CHOSEN: in this view, the workspace **IS VERBALIZABLE BECAUSE THE MODEL'S OUTPUT SPACE IS VERBAL**, and the format in which it broadcasts intermediate results to itself **IS SHAPED BY THE FORMAT IN WHICH IT MUST EVENTUALLY ACT**. The property named in the title is explained by the shape of the output channel rather than by anything about the representation

span.label: It can only name concepts that happen to be single tokens in the vocabulary.

span.label: The readout is a flat bag of concepts and cannot show how they are bound or structured together.

span.label: `J-space component`, and `in` / `aligned with` - A PAPER STIPULATING NOT ONLY A NOUN BUT THE PREPOSITIONS APPLIED TO IT: `Quotation withheld` THE SECOND SENTENCE IS THE UNUSUAL ONE. A term can be defined and still be misread through the spatial metaphor its own name invites - `in` a space normally means membership, and here it is stipulated to mean APPROXIMATION. The authors fix the preposition because the noun alone would not have stopped the wrong reading.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: `J-space` - A NAME BORROWED FROM LINEAR ALGEBRA FOR SOMETHING THAT IS NOT A SUBSPACE. `THIS UNION OF CONES IS THE J-SPACE.` The suffix `-space` invites every habit a reader has about spans, bases and dimensions, and the object is **a union of polyhedral cones** - closed under nonnegative combination only. **The paper says so plainly and the name still does the misleading**, which is mechanism 28's shape (a name whose extension is wrong) arriving through a suffix rather than through a stem.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: `J-space component` - DEFINED BY WHAT IT CAN BE WRITTEN AS, NOT BY A PROJECTION. `Quotation withheld` In a subspace, `component` means an orthogonal projection and is unique. Here it means a best sparse nonnegative approximation - **the same word, a different mathematical object, and the difference follows directly from J-space not being a space.** **NO EDGE PROPOSED, AND THIS REFUSAL IS DIFFERENT FROM THE OTHERS TONIGHT.** `part-of` is the RIGHT type here; the paper simply never asserts the containment in words. I searched every sentence mentioning `J-space` for an accepted containment cue and the closest is a QUESTION - `what fraction of the model's representational space BELONGS TO the J-space?` - which asks the thing rather than claiming it. The relation was my inference from the definition, not the paper's statement, and the gate caught exactly that.
